focus_areas: Structural integrity of the caliper-rotor interface
Realism of the rust and wear textures on the metal surfaces
Geometric correctness of the lug nut pattern and hub assembly
Nature of the blue ring artifact on the rotor
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the blue ring on the rotor; determine if it's a plausible physical feature (e.g., a protective coating or marker) or an AI generation artifact. Verify that the caliper's mounting points are physically logical and not just 'floating' near the rotor. Check if the rust texture is consistent across the metal surfaces or if it looks pasted on.
image_description: A close-up view of a vehicle wheel assembly, specifically focusing on the brake system. The image shows a rusty, solid metal rotor (disc) mounted to a hub with lug nuts. A teal/green painted caliper housing is visible at the top left, clamping over the rotor edge. There is a distinct blue ring or marking on the outer face of the rotor. The surrounding suspension components and tire sidewall are also visible. The components show signs of wear, rust, and dirt.

expert_testimonies.reason: To verify the caliper is correctly positioned over the rotor edge and that the rotor sits flush with the hub, checking for structural melting or floating parts.
To confirm the specific mechanical components match the 'disk brake' class label and distinguish from drum brakes or other wheel parts.
To ensure the hydraulic lines connect logically to the caliper without fusion or broken topology, and that the caliper is a single coherent object.
